- Second click: blob (1,3), row [G,G,G,B,B,G,G] → marker at (1,5): the first G to the right, skipping over blobs.
- This click: blob (1,5), row [G,G,G,G,G,B,G] → to the right: (1,6) is G. But the marker appeared at (3,5) below!
Hmm. So the rule is different. Maybe the marker appears in the direction of the nearest blob? No...
Maybe the marker appears at the position where the blob "falls" under gravity? Like, the blob falls down? (1,5) → falls to (3,5)? But (2,5) has a blob... it should stop at (1,5)? No, it's already there.
Wait — maybe the marker indicates where the blob will move if clicked again, and that direction is... hmm.
Let me think: maybe the marker appears in the direction of the nearest other blob? Blob (1,5): nearest blob is (2,5) below. Marker at (3,5) = one past (2,5)? Like "jump over the blob below"?
First click: blob (1,1): nearest blob is (1,2) to the right (adjacent). Marker at (1,3) = one past (1,2) ✓.
Second click: blob (1,3): nearest blob is (1,4) to the right. Marker at (1,5) = one past (1,4) ✓.
Third click: blob (1,5): nearest blob is (2,5) below (distance 1). Marker at (3,5) = one past (2,5) ✓!!
So the rule: the marker appears one cell past the nearest adjacent blob (the blob it will merge with), i.e., the marker is at the position where the selected blob will land after jumping over the nearest blob.
And clicking the marker: the selected blob + the blob jumped over merge into the marker's position.
First merge: selected (1,1), jumped over (1,2), merged at (1,3) ✓.
Second merge: selected (1,3), jumped over (1,4), merged at (1,5) ✓.
So now: selected (1,5), marker at (3,5), jumped over (2,5). If I click the marker: (1,5) and (2,5) merge at (3,5)!
This is a vertical merge.
So the mechanic: click a blob → it jumps over the nearest blob (in the direction of the nearest blob?) and the marker shows the landing spot. Click the marker → they merge there.
Hmm, but which blob is "the nearest"? In the case of blob (1,5): the blobs are (2,5) below [distance 1], (4,5) below [distance 3]. Nearest = (2,5) below. ✓.
In the case of blob (1,1): the blobs are (1,2) right [distance 1], (1,4) [distance 3], (2,5), (4,5). Nearest = (1,2) right ✓.
So the rule: the nearest blob (probably 4-directional adjacency / Chebyshev distance).
Now the goal: probably to merge all the blobs into one. Currently 3 blobs: (1,5), (2,5), (4,5).
If I click the marker at (3,5): (1,5)+(2,5) merge at (3,5). Then the blobs: (3,5), (4,5).
Next, select (3,5): nearest blob (4,5) below, marker at (5,5). Click → merge at (5,5). One blob remaining at (5,5).
Then... if only one blob remains, does the level clear? Or does it need to be at a specific position? Let's try it.
Alternatively, select (4,5): nearest (3,5) above, marker at (2,5). Merge at (2,5).
Either way, 2 blobs → 1 blob.
Let me click the marker at (3,5) = pixel center (31, 42).
